title: Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: effective residual comparisons
summary: Starting from unconditional modularity over ℚ, this continuation gives effective bounds on residual coincidences, exact-conductor comparison curves retaining rational two-torsion, sharp weight-two newspace dimension bounds, uniform irreducibility in two-torsion families, and restricted surjectivity for non-CM curves with rational cyclic isogenies. It keeps coefficient fields, primes above the residual characteristic and all local conductor hypotheses visible.
readme: The definitive document is research/blueprint/readmes/EllipticCurveModularityPartII.md. EC.1–EC.6 plan the effective comparison route of Bennett–Siksek. Kraus uses the exact prime-to-ℓ residual conductor and Serre weight two. The three independent continuations combined by the queue are assigned explicitly in the packet’s split proposal. This roadmap extends R29 without feeding uniform irreducibility back into its fixed-curve proof. All mathematical carriers and general modularity, local conductor and Hecke theory are imported from their existing owners.

stages.title: Thresholds and sharp newspace dimensions
stages.description:
**Kraus rationality threshold.** For positive N, μ(N)=[SL₂(ℤ):Γ₀(N)] and g⁺(N)=dimℂ S₂(Γ₀(N))new, define krausF(N)=(√(μ(N)/6)+1)^(2g⁺(N)), as a real number.

**Kraus two-torsion threshold.** For positive N define krausG(N)=(√(μ(lcm(4,N))/6)+1)^2, using the full level lcm(4,N), as a real number.

**Kraus comparison threshold.** For positive N define krausH(N)=max(krausF(N),krausG(N)).

**Martin’s sharp weight-two dimension bound.** For every positive N, 12g⁺(N)≤N+1. Equality holds exactly when N=35 or N is prime with N≡11 mod 12.

stages.title: Removed-prime exponent bounds
stages.description:
**Effective congruence norm bound.** Let K be a number field of degree d, x∈𝒪K nonzero, λ a prime above the rational prime ℓ, and x∈λ. If |σ(x)|≤B for every embedding σ:K→ℂ and B≥0, then ℓ≤|NormK/ℚ(x)|≤B^d.

**Removed-prime exponent bound.** Let E/ℚ have conductor M and minimal discriminant Δ, ℓ≥3 prime with E[ℓ] irreducible, and M₀ the reduced level of R20.6. If p≠ℓ is prime, p∥M and ℓ divides ordp(Δ), then ℓ≤(√p+1)^((M₀+1)/6).

stages.title: Rationality and exact-conductor realization
stages.description:
**Finite-prime rationality recognition.** For a normalized weight-two trivial-character newform f of level N, if c_q∈ℤ for every prime q≤μ(N)/6, then every coefficient c_n is in ℤ.

**Small-prime integrality above the Kraus threshold.** Let E/ℚ have irreducible E[ℓ], Serre weight 2, ℓ≥5 prime, and residual conductor N. For a weight-two trivial-character newform f realizing E[ℓ] at N, if ℓ>krausF(N), then c_q∈ℤ for all primes q≤μ(N)/6.

**Rational newform comparison curve.** For a normalized weight-two trivial-character newform f of exact level N with all coefficients in ℤ, there exists an elliptic curve F/ℚ of exact conductor N with a_q(F)=c_q at good primes. If f realizes irreducible E[ℓ], then F[ℓ]≅E[ℓ] over ℚ.

**Kraus’s rational comparison theorem.** For E/ℚ, prime ℓ≥5, irreducible E[ℓ] of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N, ℓ>krausF(N) implies there is F/ℚ of exact conductor N with F[ℓ]≅E[ℓ].

stages.title: Full rational two-torsion realization
stages.description:
**Finite recognition of point counts modulo four.** For E/ℚ of conductor N, 4 divides #E(𝔽q) at every prime q∤2N iff it does so for all such q≤μ(lcm(4,N))/6.

**Small-prime point-count transfer.** Under Kraus Theorem 3, assume E has full rational 2-torsion and ℓ>krausG(N). For each prime q∤2N with q≤μ(lcm(4,N))/6, E has good reduction at q, and a_q(E)=a_q(F), hence 4 divides #F(𝔽q).

**Two-isogeny repair of rational two-torsion.** If E/ℚ satisfies 4|#E(𝔽q) for all but finitely many good odd q, then E is ℚ-isogenous by degree 1 or 2 to a curve F with full rational 2-torsion. For odd ℓ this isogeny preserves E[ℓ] and the conductor.

**Kraus’s full-two-torsion realization.** If E/ℚ has full rational 2-torsion, ℓ≥5 is prime, E[ℓ] is irreducible of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N, and ℓ>krausH(N), then some F/ℚ has exact conductor N, full rational 2-torsion, and F[ℓ]≅E[ℓ].

**Reduced-level adapter for Kraus’s theorem.** In an application with reduced level M₀ from R20.6, Kraus’s full-two-torsion theorem applies at M₀ only after establishing Serre weight 2 and N(E[ℓ])=M₀. In particular, for ℓ≥5 and ℓ∤M, local conductor comparison gives N(E[ℓ])=M₀; weight 2 must still be checked (for example by finite flatness at ℓ).

stages.title: Uniform two-torsion irreducibility
stages.description:
**Mazur’s prime-isogeny theorem.** If E/ℚ admits a cyclic rational isogeny of prime degree r, then r∈{2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,37,43,67,163}. For non-CM E the possibilities are {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,37}.

**Two-torsion isogeny exclusions.** For every prime ℓ≥11, no elliptic curve over ℚ admits a cyclic rational 2ℓ-isogeny. For every prime ℓ≥7, none admits a cyclic rational 4ℓ-isogeny.

**Two-torsion kernel transport.** For odd prime ℓ, if E/ℚ has a rational cyclic ℓ-subgroup and a rational point of order 2, it admits a rational cyclic 2ℓ-isogeny. If all E[2] is rational, some curve isogenous to E admits a rational cyclic 4ℓ-isogeny.

**Irreducibility with full rational two-torsion.** If E/ℚ has full rational 2-torsion and ℓ≥7 is prime, E[ℓ] is irreducible over 𝔽ℓ; since it is odd, it is absolutely irreducible.

**Irreducibility with a rational two-torsion point.** If E/ℚ has a rational point of order 2 and ℓ≥11 is prime, E[ℓ] is irreducible over 𝔽ℓ and absolutely irreducible.

stages.title: Rational-isogeny uniformity
stages.description:
**Potential good reduction in the nonsplit Cartan case.** If p≥5 is prime and ρ̄E,p(Gℚ) is contained in the normalizer of a nonsplit Cartan, then E has potentially good reduction at each rational prime q with q≢±1 mod p, and also at q=p.

**Chen’s isogeny at rational-isogeny level.** For r∈{1,2,3,5,7,13} and prime p∉{1,2,3,5,7,13}, the Jacobian of X₀(r)×X(1)Xns⁺(p) is ℚ-isogenous to the p-new quotient of Jac(X₀⁺(rp²)), by a correspondence commuting with T_n for gcd(n,p)=1.

**Rank-zero winding quotient.** For r∈{2,3,5,7,13} and prime p outside that set, J₀,ns⁺(r,p) has a nonzero optimal ℚ-quotient A with A(ℚ) finite and kernel stable under every T_n with gcd(n,p)=1.

**Cuspidal formal immersion at isogeny level.** For r∈{2,3,5,7,13}, p outside that set and a prime q≠p with q≡±1 mod p, the Abel–Jacobi map to the rank-zero quotient A on X₀,ns⁺(r,p), after choosing a cusp and its local integral model, is a formal immersion at that cusp in characteristic q; a rational section specializing there has torsion image in A.

**Prime-integrality of the isogeny j-invariant.** For r∈Σ={2,3,5,7,13}, prime p∉Σ, and E/ℚ admitting a cyclic rational r-isogeny with mod-p image in a nonsplit Cartan normalizer, j(E)∈ℤ[1/p].

**Integrality of the isogeny j-invariant.** For r∈{2,3,5,7,13}, prime p∉{2,3,5,7,13}, and non-CM E/ℚ with an r-isogeny and mod-p image in a nonsplit Cartan normalizer, j(E) is an integer.

**Integral j-values at genus-zero isogeny levels.** For r∈{2,3,5,7,13}, choose t on X₀(r) so j=f_r(t)/t, where f₂=(t+16)^3, f₃=(t+27)(t+3)^3, f₅=(t²+10t+5)^3, f₇=(t²+5t+1)^3(t²+13t+49), f₁₃=(t⁴+7t³+20t²+19t+1)^3(t²+5t+13). Every noncuspidal rational point with integral j has nonzero integral t dividing f_r(0).

**Large proper images are nonsplit Cartan images.** For non-CM E/ℚ and prime p>37, if ρ̄E,p is not surjective onto GL₂(𝔽p), its image is contained in a nonsplit Cartan normalizer.

**Surjectivity under quadratic twisting.** For odd prime p and non-CM E/ℚ, quadratic twisting preserves surjectivity of the mod-p representation. Thus for a fixed non-CM rational j, surjectivity at p can be tested on one representative curve.

**Finite rational-j Galois-image certificates.** For every non-CM j in the integral sets S₂∪S₃∪S₅∪S₇∪S₁₃ from the divisor enumeration, and every non-CM j in S₁₁={−11·131³,−2¹⁵,−11²}, S₁₇={−17²·101³/2,−17·373³/2¹⁷}, S₃₇={−7·137³·2083³,−7·11³}, an explicit curve with that j has surjective mod-p representation for every prime p>37.

**Lemos’s rational-isogeny uniformity theorem.** If E/ℚ is non-CM, meaning Endℚ̄(E)=ℤ, and admits a nontrivial cyclic rational isogeny, then ρ̄E,p(Gℚ)=GL₂(𝔽p) for every prime p>37.
